topic: Criminal Law: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and CrPC
description: This module covers the procedural aspects of criminal law, highlighting the transition from the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973 to the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. It focuses on the introduction of time-bound justice, digital transformation of legal procedures, and enhanced forensic and citizen-centric reforms.

key_points: The Transition: The BNSS 2023 replaces the CrPC 1973, shifting the legislative focus from mere 'procedure' to 'citizen protection' (Nagarik Suraksha).
Strict Timelines: To combat judicial delays, BNSS introduces mandatory timelines. For instance, a judgment must be pronounced within 30 days (extendable by 45 days) from the completion of arguments.

Zero FIR Formalized: It statutorily mandates that a police station must register an FIR for a cognizable offense regardless of its territorial jurisdiction (Zero FIR) and forward it to the concerned police station within 24 hours.
Electronic FIR (e-FIR): BNSS allows the filing of information for FIRs through electronic communication, provided it is signed by the informant within three days.
Digital Trials: All trials, inquiries, and proceedings, including the issuance of summons, examination of witnesses, and recording of evidence, can now be conducted in electronic mode.
Search and Seizure Transparency: To prevent evidence tampering and ensure accountability, the BNSS mandates the audio-video recording of search operations and seizures of property.

forensics_bail_absconders.concept: Forensics, Undertrial Bail, and Proclaimed Offenders
key_points: Mandatory Forensics: For offenses punishable with imprisonment of seven years or more, forensic investigation is now mandatory. Experts must visit the crime scene to collect evidence and record the process.

Bail for First-Time Offenders: Offering relief to undertrials, BNSS stipulates that a first-time offender must be released on bail if they have undergone detention for one-third of the maximum imprisonment period specified for the offense.

Trial in Absentia: If a proclaimed offender absconds to evade trial and there is no immediate prospect of arresting them, the BNSS allows the court to conduct the trial and pronounce the judgment in their absence.

questions.question: To ensure transparency and prevent allegations of planting evidence, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) mandates which of the following during a police search and seizure operation?

options.A: Presence of a High Court Judge
options.B: Audio-video recording of the search and seizure process
options.C: Live broadcasting of the search on national television
options.D: Written permission from the Chief Minister

questions.explanation: To ensure fairness and transparency, BNSS mandates the audio-video recording of searches and seizures, including the preparation of the seizure list and signing by witnesses.

questions.question: The police arrive at a crime scene involving an offense that carries a maximum punishment of 10 years of imprisonment. According to the new BNSS 2023, what procedural step is now statutorily mandatory for the investigating team?

options.A: They must arrest the suspect immediately without an FIR.
options.B: They must mandate a forensic investigation and have forensic experts visit the crime scene to collect evidence.
options.C: They must transfer the case to the CBI within 24 hours.
options.D: They must release all witnesses on personal bonds.

questions.explanation: BNSS mandates that for any offense punishable with imprisonment of seven years or more, it is compulsory for forensic experts to visit the crime scene to collect forensic evidence.

questions.question: How does the BNSS address the issue of overcrowded prisons and prolonged pre-trial detention for 'first-time offenders' compared to the older CrPC provisions?

options.A: It states that first-time offenders cannot be arrested under any circumstances.
options.B: It mandates that a first-time offender must be released on bond if they have served one-third of the maximum period of imprisonment specified for the offense.
options.C: It requires first-time offenders to pay a fine instead of serving any jail time, regardless of the crime.
options.D: It increases the detention period for first-time offenders to deter future crimes.

questions.explanation: Under the CrPC, an undertrial was generally eligible for bail after serving half the maximum sentence. BNSS introduces a more lenient approach for first-time offenders, allowing their release on bond after they have undergone detention for one-third of the maximum prescribed imprisonment.
